sessions.description: Connecting environments across clouds used to be the part everyone dreaded. In this 90-minute hands-on lab, you’ll do it yourself — standing up a private, low-latency Interconnect between OCI and AWS (with Azure and Google Cloud patterns covered) and watching workloads on either side talk as if they were next door. You’ll configure the connection with OCI FastConnect, verify throughput and latency, apply the networking and security controls that make it production-ready, and understand the split-stack model: apps in your hyperscaler, Oracle data and services in OCI, no data movement and no egress tolls. Leave with the plumbing working and a reusable pattern, so your team can stop worrying about connectivity and start driving value.

sessions.description: Master the principles of Zero Trust security and apply them across OCI to ensure no user, device, or workload is implicitly trusted. Through hands-on labs, you'll implement continuous verification using OCI Identity Domains, enforce least-privilege access with IAM policies, segment networks with Security Lists and Network Firewalls, and protect sensitive data using OCI Vault and Data Safe. You'll leverage Cloud Guard and Security Zones to detect misconfigurations, automate threat responses, and enforce security postures in real time. By the end of the course, you'll have the skills to design and operate a Zero Trust architecture on OCI, verifying every request and securing critical assets at every layer of the stack.

questions.q: What should be standardized first, and what can be phased?
questions.why: Ask about process design, migration dependencies, initial scope, pilot sequencing, cutover criteria and adoption. Compare the customer’s context before applying its approach.

questions.q: Who owns each integration from business event through recovery?
questions.why: Explore boundaries across eCommerce, ERP and healthcare systems: API or event contracts, source of truth, adapters and protocols, identity, retries, reconciliation, observability and incident ownership.

questions.q: What data must be ready before an AI pilot is credible?
questions.why: Ask about product, supplier, order and inventory data, freshness, provenance, access controls, test cases and how errors or missing data affect the workflow.

questions.q: How would we evaluate an AI workflow beyond the demonstration?
questions.why: Compare accuracy, completion rate, exceptions, approval policy, user effort, service impact and rollback. Request current availability and distinguish shipped functionality from roadmap items.

questions.q: Which shared metrics would change an operational decision?
questions.why: Discuss order fulfillment, inventory availability, procurement and service-risk measures; define calculation ownership, refresh needs, external data and the handoff from insight to action.

questions.q: How do teams sustain adoption and release quality?
questions.why: Ask how customers onboard users, measure actual use, test critical integrations, manage quarterly changes and decide whether a new capability earns a place in the backlog.
